title: Red Fort

terrainReference.basis: Original elevation at the Chandni Chowk approach west of the Lahori barbican.

mapIdentity.provider: OpenStreetMap named fort, wall lines and gates, verified against the Archeological Survey of India and the 1911 plan.
mapIdentity.scope: The named Red Fort and exact current fortification rings and centerlines establish the main wall circuit independently of the wider UNESCO boundary. Named building and garden ways place both gates and the landmark Mughal buildings. The 1911 plan corroborates the durable perimeter, gate and bastion layout.

note: The Archaeological Survey of India describes the irregular octagon, red sandstone walls and gateways, marble waterfront palaces, and nine front arches of Diwan-i-Am. The period Bourne photograph establishes the layered Lahori Gate, octagonal turrets, parapets, and open domed chhatris. The exact 1911 Qualla plan and official accounts control the shared site geometry.
